unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the corpus sanctions writing a read form with the source's morpheme separator removed, and whether a read form occurring nowhere in the running text may be presented as a quotation. Three instances stand in this cluster: one read form at Ezek.44.5 and two at Ezek.44.24. Each is recorded here as a site with its verse; none is adjudicated and none of the three non-witness strings is reproduced.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If the convention is not sanctioned, three quotations in this cluster rest on strings the witness does not carry; if it is sanctioned, they are correct as written. The normalizer's dry run cannot settle it because it buckets read forms as their own class and returns no defect.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether a row must disclose a variant site its span merely covers, or only one a quotation binds to. Two rows here omit disclosure: Ezek.45.3 and Ezek.45.5 in one span, Ezek.46.9 and Ezek.46.15 in the other. The variant layer's own note states span coverage as the trigger and 54 of the 59 rows in the book that cover such a site disclose it, so the corpus norm is clear; but this lens's instruction names quotation binding.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Under the quotation-binding reading only the Ezek.46.15 omission is a defect, because the row's closing quotation contains that variant's written form. Under the span-coverage reading all four omissions are. Both challenges are written to hold under either reading, but the severity of the Ezek.45.3/Ezek.45.5 pair depends on which reading governs.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The severity band for a comma-placed dateline denial. The governing rule calls such a denial a rewording order and never a pass, which reads as a hard form defect, but the fact denied is true in both instances found here, so both are recorded at medium as form defects rather than as false claims.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If the rule is meant to carry the higher band whenever it fires, the two comma-placed denials in this cluster - the year-word denial and the homograph denial - should move up a band.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Three short English phrases in this cluster, written in straight single quotes as glosses, are also verbatim translation wording at their cited verse. The corpus's own quote check looks for curly single quotes, so straight-quoted verbatim wording is outside its coverage. None is charged against a row here, because the corpus convention marks a translation quotation by a double-curly delimiter plus an in-field translation reference and treats a straight-quoted phrase as a gloss, and each of the three is short enough to be the natural rendering of the Hebrew it glosses.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If the gloss/quotation boundary is meant to be drawn by content rather than by delimiter, three phrases here are undelimited translation quotations without their in-field reference, and the same class stands undetected across the corpus rather than only in this cluster.

e19_selfreport: I ran no listing, no glob, no recursive search and no directory existence test at any point. Every file I opened was named by exact path in my launch message or in my brief, or was a file I had just written to a path my launch message named. My private scratch is a uniquely named subdirectory of my own session scratchpad, created without being tested for. I wrote nothing under the lane worktree, wrote no receipt, ran no git command and did not touch the registry.
